F2-Q1.question: What should we prioritize for the Nov 11 outage?
F2-Q1.answer:
**Priority 1: add a couch roll DS bearing change to the Nov 11 scope.**
- The outage scope has only WO 26108274 (rebuild couch roll seal strips), and its parts are not reserved. I found no WO for the bearing itself.
- Couch roll DS vibration has climbed every day since about Oct 16. It was 0.068 in/s on Oct 10–13 and 0.236 in/s on Oct 31, now above the 0.15 Alert limit [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
- Bonvoy shows the rise as about 20% a day and 13.5σ above its band, flagged 15 days running [Bonvoy PM1:COUCH_DS_VIB 2026-10-31].
- The Oct 14 Keel route did not catch it [KV-VR-261014]. This matches the earlier couch roll bearing failure that happened between routes [RCFA-SM-25-001].
- A straight-line extrapolation of the last 7 days (about 0.014 in/s per day) reaches the 0.40 Danger limit around Nov 11. The rise is speeding up, so it could arrive sooner.
- Ask Keel for an off-route spectrum now, and confirm bearing and lube stock. Reserve the seal strip parts too. Consider pulling the bearing change forward if vibration keeps climbing.

**Priority 2: reel drum DS bearing, WO 26107420.**
- Vibration is 0.426 in/s, above the 0.40 Danger limit. Bonvoy doesn't flag it because its baseline has moved up with the defect [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
- The bearing (22238 CCK/W33) is on order with an ETA of Nov 5. The expedite action SM-0201 (Quentin Adeyemi) is 16 days overdue.
- Confirm delivery on Nov 5. This job is 10 h, so it needs a crew and a plan alongside the other long jobs.

**Priority 3: refiner plates, WO 26108904 (REF 1) and WO 26108911 (REF 2).**
- Parts are not reserved on either WO. Only one Ridgeway plate set is on hand for two refiners.
- The order for a second set (SM-0241) is 3 days overdue, with the quote requested Oct 21.
- REF 2 plates are only 30 days into an 84-day target life. Specific energy has been high for 12 days and Ridgeway has written it up [RR-FV-261026]. REF 1 is 72 days in.
- Decide which refiner gets the one set. REF 2 is wearing fastest, but it may be the earlier-failing set, so check the cause before changing it. Chase the order.

**Other items to resolve**
- 2nd section PV fan belts and sheaves, WO 26108281, has no parts reserved.
- The overdue RCFA actions on the dryer drive grease review (SM-0207) and the shower strainer on the outage clean list (SM-0195) relate to scheduled work. The strainer is relevant to the HP shower nozzle change, WO 26108743.
- RCFA-SM-26-029 (dryer driveshaft) has an action due Nov 5, and RCFA-SM-26-028 (2nd press drive) has one due Nov 2.

**Scope load**
- The scope totals about 150 h across 22 WOs against a 20 h outage, so crew and sequencing will drive what actually gets done. I did not check crew assignments.

F1-Q1.question: Why did we change the 2nd press top felt early in May?
F1-Q1.answer:
The 2nd press top felt was changed early on **May 19**, not at the start of May. It was changed because it filled up at about 3 weeks. The felt had run 33 days against a 42-day target. [WO 26105306]

**What the crew saw before the change** [BUS 2026-05-04]:
- Uhle box vacuum was up 4.6 inHg.
- Press exit solids were down 1.8 points.
- 4th section steam was at its limit on 34 Super.
- There were repeated press-area sheet break days: 4 breaks on May 2 and May 10, and 5 on May 14. [BUS 2026-05-10] [BUS 2026-05-14]

The change was logged as an unplanned felt change. It took 7.5 h (450 min). [Downtime DT-260519-0344]

**Likely root cause:** the HP shower nozzles were plugged, so the felt wasn't being conditioned. The Spraywell audit on May 13 found 22% of the nozzles plugged. [SW-SA-260513] [RCFA-SM-26-016]

The RCFA is still open. Two of its actions are done: the weekly nozzle check by operations [Action SM-0141] and cleaning the HP shower supply strainer every outage [Action SM-0139]. Action SM-0138 is late and still in progress. It adds the Uhle vacuum rate-of-rise to the Bonvoy watch list and was due 2026-07-15.

The runs since then were normal: 50, 41 and 41 days, plus the current one.

Marlow's used felt analysis is MP-FA-260526. I only saw its header, not the fill measurements.

H1.question: Overlay Uhle vacuum on the 2nd press top felt for the April felt against the two felts before it, by days on the machine.
H1.answer:
The April felt (installed 2026-04-15) filled much faster than the two felts before it. It was removed early, on day 33.

- **Start:** All three felts began at about 9.35 inHg once running (day 2–3).
- **Jan 21 felt:** It rose about 2.5 inHg over its 41 days, reaching 11.84 on day 41.
- **Mar 4 felt:** It followed almost the same path, reaching 11.91 on day 41.
- **April felt:** It tracked the other two until about day 12 (9.72). It then pulled away, reaching 11.24 by day 20 and 12.45 by day 25. By day 33 it was at 14.36, about 5 inHg above its start.
- **Gaps in the chart:** Outage days and days with a stop (daily minimum of 0) are left blank. That includes the first two days after each install.

The felt record says it was changed early, at 79% of its 42-day target. Its comment cites press solids down 1.8 points and 4th section steam at its limit on 34 Super. It also says 22% of the HP shower nozzles were plugged in the Spraywell audit on May 13. The plugged showers fit the faster filling, but I haven't pulled the audit itself to confirm it.

The comparison felts also had normal removal comments, and one had edge filling cleaned with the HP shower at mid-life.

H5.question: Did the May 19 felt change fix the press? Chart the week before against the week after.
H5.answer:
**Yes, mostly. The May 19 change of the 2nd press top felt fixed the press symptoms, but the 4th section steam pressure is creeping back up.** The felt was pulled early at 3 weeks for filling. The 7.5 h change was on WO 26105306 [Shift Report PM1-SHIFT-2026-05-19-D].

The chart compares the two weeks day by day. I left out May 12–13 because stops that week distort the daily averages. The "before" figures below use May 14–18.

- **Uhle vacuum (2nd press top):** It was climbing from 13.4 to 14.4 inHg before the change. It dropped to about 9.5 inHg and stayed flat for the week after [pi_daily PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC].
- **Press exit solids:** They were drifting down from 42.7% to 42.1%. After the change they ran about 44.1%, roughly 1.7 points higher [pi_daily PM1:PRESS_SOLIDS].
- **Dryer steam:** Steam per ton fell from about 1.63 to 1.51 t/t [production].
- **4th section steam pressure:** It averaged about 127 psig before and about 117 psig in the first days after. It was back to 125–128 psig by May 25–26, so watch it [pi_daily PM1:DRY4_STEAM_P].
- **Output:** Tons per day rose from about 687 to about 729, and breaks fell from about 3.0 to 0.7 per day [production]. This is a short sample, and I didn't adjust for grade mix.

**Root cause:** The Spraywell audit of May 13 found 22% of the 2nd press top HP shower nozzles plugged [SW-SA-260513]. The shift handover says the nozzles were cleaned, but the felt was still filling at that point. The later Spraywell audits (Aug 5, Oct 21) list the shower under the same table, but I only saw the first line of each report. I didn't confirm the nozzle percentages. Check that the shower is still clean, or the new felt will fill early too.

The next 2nd press top felts were changed on schedule at 41 days, so the early-fill problem did not recur [position_life p2-felt-top].

H2.question: Chart REF 1 against REF 2 specific energy since the Sep 30 outage. At this rate, where will REF 2 be on Nov 11?
H2.answer:
At the current rate, REF 2 reaches about 92 kWh/t on Nov 11. That is roughly 50% above where it started after the Sep 30 plate change. This is a straight-line extrapolation, not a forecast.

- **REF 2:** It ran flat at about 57.5–58.7 kWh/t from Oct 1 to Oct 8. It has climbed almost every day since, to 81.3 kWh/t on Oct 31. The rise since Oct 8 is about 0.97 kWh/t per day, and the last 10 days are about the same (71.4 to 81.3). Eleven more days at that rate adds about 10.7, which gives roughly 92. If the climb keeps steepening, it would be higher.
- **REF 1:** It is steady at about 60–62 kWh/t, with a slight drift up to 62.75 on Oct 31. REF 1 began the period about 2 kWh/t above REF 2. REF 2 is now about 19 kWh/t above REF 1.

The data doesn't show why REF 2 is climbing. The previous REF 2 plate set was recorded as 85% worn at 12 weeks, against a normal of about 60% [Ridgeway report RR-PL-260930-B]. The current set is only 30 days old, which is 36% of its 84-day target. A climb this fast on new plates is unusual. Earlier sets showed steady energy per ton to the end of their runs.

The next outage is Nov 11, so the plates would run to then. I'd have Ridgeway check the REF 2 plates, and check plate gap and load against REF 1, before the climb gets worse.

H3.question: Did the 3rd section syphon differential warn us before each rotary joint leak? Show the 10 days before each one.
H3.answer:
**Partly.** The syphon differential (PM1:DRY3_DP) dropped below its normal band before two of the three leaks. The third leak got almost no warning. All three were seal-kit changes on the 3rd section DS rotary joint, and none had an RCFA.

- **Jan 6 leak [WO 26102009]:** Bonvoy flagged DP low on Jan 4 (4 h), Jan 5 (13 h) and Jan 6 (9 h). That is about 2 days of warning [Bonvoy PM1:DRY3_DP 2026-01-04 to 01-06]. The daily average fell from about 4.2–4.3 psi to 2.4–3.7 psi, but the dip started around Dec 30. Several of those days also show 0 psi minimums, so the early part is confounded by stoppages.
- **Jun 23 leak [WO 26106237]:** This was the clearest warning. DP was low for 4 straight days, Jun 20 to 23, flagged for 11, 18, 14 and 14 h. The daily average dropped from about 4.2 psi to 2.5–3.0 psi.
- **Oct 2 leak [WO 26108638]:** This had little useful warning.
  - There was a 3 h low flag on Sep 21, 11 days before, which is too early to link.
  - The next flags were Oct 1 (11 h) and Oct 2 (3 h), the day before and the day of the leak.
  - The Sep 30–Oct 1 outage sits in the middle of the window and distorts the readings.

DP drifts with grade, and the daily averages are not corrected for that. In Oct, Sep 23–25 averaged about 3.2–3.4 psi with no flag. I would trust Bonvoy's grade-aware flags over the raw averages.

A sustained low-DP flag of 2–4 days is a usable early sign of this failure. It gives only days of notice, not weeks.

The review action is open: [Action: SM-0230, Root cause review of 3rd section rotary joint leaks, due 2026-11-20, not started]. Each leak cost 2.4–2.9 h of unplanned downtime.

F5-Q1.question: Which repeat failures don't have an RCFA?
F5-Q1.answer:
Only one repeat failure in the last 12 months (1 Nov 2025 to 31 Oct 2026) has no RCFA: the 3rd section rotary joint (DS). It stopped the machine 3 times for a total of 8 h, all for "Rotary joint leak". The stops were on 2026-01-06 and 2026-10-02, plus one between them. [WO 26102009, 26106237, 26108638] [repeat_stops 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31]

The other eight repeat-stop items each have at least one RCFA. Four have fewer RCFAs than stops, so some individual stops may not have been analysed. This is inferred from the counts, not checked event by event.
- 1st press bottom felt: 4 stops, 2 RCFAs (RCFA-SM-26-015 and -025).
- 1st press top felt HP shower: 3 stops, 1 RCFA (RCFA-SM-26-024).
- 2nd press bottom felt: 2 stops, 1 RCFA (RCFA-SM-26-014).
- 4th section rotary joint (DS): 2 stops, 1 RCFA (RCFA-SM-26-012).

Headbox has 2 stops (side door blown off, slime build-up) and 1 RCFA, RCFA-SM-26-020. That RCFA is titled and rooted on the slime build-up, so the side-door blow-off looks uncovered.

Dryer drive lineup, pulper rotor and 2nd press drive each have an RCFA for every stop.

Having an RCFA doesn't mean the follow-up is done. Several of these RCFAs are still open with overdue actions, including RCFA-SM-26-015, -014, -024 and -026. [rcfa_status]

I'd open an RCFA on the 3rd section rotary joint first, because it has leaked three times with no analysis.

H4.question: Is the reel drum bearing temperature following the vibration? Plot both since mid-July.
H4.answer:
Yes. Temperature has followed vibration closely since mid-July, and both are still climbing.

- **Vibration:** The daily max went from about 0.064 in/s on Jul 15 to 0.431 on Oct 31. It passed Alert (0.15) around Aug 8–10 and Danger (0.40) around Oct 19. The Bonvoy Report lists it at 0.426 on Oct 31 as above Danger [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
- **Temperature:** The daily max went from about 136 °F to 169.5 °F, a rise of about 33 °F. It started climbing about when vibration did, around Jul 22–27, and has risen steadily since.
- **Tracking:** The two series move together with no lag I can see in the 3-day points. They are not perfectly proportional. Temperature rose about 33 °F while vibration rose about 6.7 times. Temperature also rose by more than 5 °F during Jul 24–Aug 26, while vibration was still below 0.25.
- **Bonvoy flags:** Bonvoy flagged both tags nearly every day from late July to about Aug 23, for example [Bonvoy PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_TEMP 2026-08-20]. The flags stopped because its baseline has moved up with the trend. The Bonvoy Report watch list notes this.
- **Cause and plan:** The Keel route on Aug 12 found an outer race defect [KV-VR-260812]. The bearing was not in stores. It was deferred from the Aug 19 outage, ordered (22238 CCK/W33, ETA Nov 5), and rescheduled for Nov 11 [WO 26107420] [Action: SM-0201].

Extrapolation: the Oct 17–31 rate is about 0.0025 in/s per day, so vibration would be roughly 0.46 in/s by Nov 11 if nothing changes. That is above the Danger limit, so the run-or-stop decision on the BUS sheet still stands [BUS 2026-09-09]. Action SM-0201 is shown as late.

I don't have a temperature alarm limit in the data. The 3-sigma limits Bonvoy used are no longer a useful guide.

P1.question: If the reel drum bearing keeps rising, will it hit Danger before Nov 11?
P1.answer:
**It has already hit Danger, so the question is no longer whether it will before Nov 11.**

- The Danger limit is 0.40 in/s (Alert is 0.15) [KV-VR-261014]. The reel drum DS bearing read 0.426 in/s on Oct 31 [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
- The daily average passed 0.40 around Oct 22–23. Hourly peaks first touched 0.405 on Oct 19 [pi_daily PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_VIB].
- Bonvoy doesn't flag it, because its baseline has moved up with the trend. It shows only on the watch list [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].

**Trend**
- It has risen steadily since early August, from 0.126 to 0.426.
- The last 9 days average about 0.003 in/s per day.
- I assumed that rate continues, which is an extrapolation. It would put the bearing near 0.46 in/s by Nov 11, 11 days away.
- Nothing in the data gives a failure level above Danger. A steady rise isn't a safe guide to when it fails.

**Cause**
- Keel found an outer race defect (BPFO with harmonics). Alert was first called on Aug 12 at 0.17 in/s, and Sep 9 and Oct 14 were also Alert [KV-VR-260812, KV-VR-260909, KV-VR-261014].
- The same bearing failed on Nov 24, 2025. That cost 2.8 h of downtime, and the crew noted it wasn't caught on the route [WO 26100945].

**Parts and plan**
- The bearing change is [WO 26107420], 10 h, set for the Nov 11 outage. It is still waiting on parts.
- The bearing (22238 CCK/W33) is on order with an ETA of Nov 5. It was deferred from the Aug 19 outage because it wasn't in stores.
- The BUS sheet asks for a run-or-stop decision at Danger [BUS 2026-10-31].

**What to do**
- Confirm the Nov 5 delivery with the supplier now. Any slip means the bearing can't be changed on Nov 11.
- Ask Keel for an off-route spectrum reading before then.
- Set stop criteria, such as a step change in the trend or a rise in bearing temperature (PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_TEMP).
- Decide whether to change it in an earlier short stop once the bearing arrives on Nov 5.
- Check that Nov 11 has enough hours. The bearing change is 10 h of a 20 h outage, and the reel scanner calibration ([WO 26108736], 6 h) is also on the reel drum.

S1.question: Do we break more on 24# than on 34 Super? Chart it.
S1.answer:
Yes, 24# breaks more than 34 Super, but only about a third more once you adjust for run time. The raw counts (395 breaks on 24# against 101 on 34 Super) mostly reflect that 24# ran far more hours.

Breaks per 100 h run, 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31:
- **24#:** 395 breaks in 5,596 h, which is 7.1 per 100 h.
- **34 Super:** 101 breaks in 1,932 h, which is 5.2 per 100 h.
- **31#:** 57 breaks in 970 h, which is 5.9 per 100 h.
- **28#:** 16 breaks in 238 h, which is 6.7 per 100 h. This is a small sample.

24# runs about 1.35 times the break rate of 34 Super. My rough Poisson estimate says that gap is larger than random variation (about 2.7 standard errors). It ignores differences in conditions between runs, so treat it as a good indication, not proof.

Time lost per break is about the same on every grade (0.77 h on 34 Super, 0.78 h on 24#). So the extra downtime on 24# comes from more breaks, not longer ones.

24# also has the most unplanned equipment downtime per hour run. It had 28 stops (119.8 h) against 9 stops (34.8 h) on 34 Super. Per hour run that is about 5.0 stops per 1,000 h on 24# against 4.7 on 34 Super, so that gap is small.

Sources: [downtime_summary by grade, 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31], [grade_hours, same period].

S2.question: Is one crew breaking more than the others? Show it on a chart.
S2.answer:
Crew B has the most breaks, but the gap is small and not clear enough to call a real difference between crews.

Sheet breaks from 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31 (569 in total):
- **Crew B:** 161 breaks, about 8.0 per 100 h run.
- **Crew C:** 146 breaks, about 7.5 per 100 h.
- **Crew D:** 140 breaks, about 7.0 per 100 h.
- **Crew A:** 122 breaks, about 6.2 per 100 h.

The mill average is about 7.15 per 100 h.

**How solid this is**
- **Run hours are estimated.** The feed doesn't give run hours per crew, so I split the year four ways and subtracted each crew's logged stop time. Crews C and A took most of the planned outage hours, which I allowed for.
- **The spread is within chance.** B is about 1.8 standard deviations above an even split and A about 1.9 below. A chi-square test on the counts gives p of roughly 0.14.
- **Grade mix is not checked.** 24# ran 64% of hours but had 69.5% of breaks, so a crew that ran more 24# could look worse without being worse. I didn't split breaks by crew and grade.
- **Break length is the same.** Every crew averages about 0.7–0.8 h per break, so no crew is slower to recover.

**Unplanned stops** don't line up with breaks. Crew D had the most unplanned downtime (12 events, 57.5 h), then B (11 events, 49.5 h), A (11 events, 35.9 h) and C (8 events, 33 h). That is too few events to rank crews.

I'd treat the breaks as a machine or grade issue rather than a crew issue. Dryer cans keep appearing in the break records, for example cans 6, 16 and 3 in late October. If you want, I can break breaks down by equipment, or by crew within each grade.

S3.question: Make a monthly chart of tons and break hours. Which month hurt most, and why?
S3.answer:
**May 2026 hurt most.** It had the most break time of any month, 52.2 h across 73 breaks. The next worst were July at 42.6 h and January at 42.3 h. May also had the lowest tons per day (655 t/d, 20,316 t for the month) apart from February's short month. Uptime was 94.1%, and only July (93.5%) was lower. Steam per ton was 1.59, the highest of the year.

Why May was bad:
- **Press-section breaks:** 24 breaks cost 28.8 h, 55% of the month's break time. At 1.2 h each they were the slowest to recover from. Dryer breaks were 25 (16.9 h) and reel breaks were 24 (6.5 h).
- **Press felt problems:** these caused most of the unplanned downtime, 23.8 h in total.
  - Two emergency felt washes cost 9 h [WO 26105138, RCFA-SM-26-014] and [WO 26105159, RCFA-SM-26-015]. The downtime notes say Uhle vacuum had been climbing and press solids falling for 16 and 26 days before.
  - An unplanned 2nd press top felt change cost 7.5 h [WO 26105306, RCFA-SM-26-016]. The felt had filled at 3 weeks, and the 4th section steam was at its limit.
  - A 1st press bottom felt blow cost 2.3 h [WO 26104942].
- **Hood exhaust fan failure:** 5.1 h on 28 May [WO 26105509, RCFA-SM-26-017]. Hood exhaust temperature and moisture had been drifting for 23 days.
- **Grade mix:** 24# ran 69% of the hours but took 58 of the 73 breaks, about 11.3 per 100 h. 34 Super and 31# were about 6 per 100 h. 24# is the grade the machine runs most, so I can't separate a 24# effect from the felt problems.

Three of the four felt and fan failures had warning trends for 2 to 4 weeks. That means they could have been caught earlier.

Two caveats:
- Break hours on the chart come from the downtime summary. The production table gives slightly different minutes in some months, for example July at 2,676 min against 2,553 min.
- Tons stay in a narrow range of about 19,600 to 21,300 t. Tons therefore don't show May as sharply as break hours do.

P2.question: When was the calender bottom roll last ground?
P2.answer:
PM1 has no calender stack, so there is no calender bottom roll and no grind record for one. The machine goes from the dryer sections to the reel and winder. Nothing in the documents or work orders mentions a calender. [SM-DWG-101]

You may mean one of the press rolls, which the roll shop does regrind. The closest match is the 2nd press bottom roll:
- It was removed on 2026-09-30 after 566 days and sent out to recover and regrind. [WO 26107805]
- Pellham Roll Service wrote the service report on it. [PR-RS-261009-p2bottom]

I haven't checked the 1st press rolls or the top rolls. Tell me which roll you want and I'll look it up.

AC-Q1.question: What actions are overdue?
AC-Q1.answer:
As of 2026-10-31, 11 actions are overdue. All are marked "In progress". The list runs from most to least overdue.

**RCFA actions**
- SM-0064: MCC room cooling check (RCFA-SM-26-007). Desmond Pike, due Apr 20, 194 days late.
- SM-0059: Install a wad detector camera at the breast roll (RCFA-SM-26-006). Fenna Gallagher, due Apr 30, 184 days late.
- SM-0135: Add Uhle vacuum rate-of-rise to the shift checks for the 1st press bottom felt (RCFA-SM-26-015). Tobias Renner, due Jun 4, 149 days late.
- SM-0145: Add hood exhaust fan belts to the monthly PM (RCFA-SM-26-017). Gloria Nakamura, due Jun 19, 134 days late.
- SM-0133: Review felt design with the felt vendor (RCFA-SM-26-014). Sunniva Brooks, due Jun 24, 129 days late.
- SM-0124: Review grease type and interval for the pulper rotor (RCFA-SM-26-013). Gloria Nakamura, due Jul 1, 122 days late.
- SM-0138: Add Uhle vacuum rate-of-rise to the Bonvoy watch list (RCFA-SM-26-016). Mei Fairbanks, due Jul 15, 108 days late.
- SM-0195: Add the shower strainer to every outage clean list (RCFA-SM-26-024). Tobias Renner, due Aug 27, 65 days late.
- SM-0207: Review grease type and interval for the dryer drive lineup (RCFA-SM-26-026). Gloria Nakamura, due Oct 29, 2 days late.

**Outage-related (most urgent, because the Nov 11 outage is close)**
- SM-0201: Expedite the reel drum DS bearing (22238 CCK/W33), ETA Nov 5. Quentin Adeyemi, due Oct 15, 16 days late. It was deferred from Aug 19 because it wasn't in stores [WO 26107420].
- SM-0241: Order a second set of 34" LC refiner plates. Quentin Adeyemi, due Oct 28, 3 days late. Only one Ridgeway set is on hand, REF 2 is wearing fast, and both refiners are due Nov 11. The quote was requested Oct 21.

**Patterns**
- Eight of the 11 are RCFA follow-ups, and each is more than 60 days late except SM-0207.
- Gloria Nakamura owns three of them and Tobias Renner owns two. Quentin Adeyemi owns both outage items.
- Four of the late RCFA actions cite WO 26100833 as the work order.

I'd start with SM-0201 and SM-0241, since the Nov 11 outage depends on them.
